name: instance-override-policy-channels-batch3
title: tests(instance): pin device/process/kernel policy override arms (batch 3)
body:
### What
Pins the third batch of `apply_override_inner` match arms: `contract.devices.read/.write/.create`, `contract.process.signals` and `contract.kernel.proc_read` each apply their parsed list to the matching field, and a non-empty device create list flips `filesystem_device_nodes`.

### Why it matters
Each arm is an independent security-policy channel. A deleted arm silently ignores the operator's override while returning success, so a device or kernel rule would never take effect. The existing suite pins batch 1 (#370) and the filesystem batch (#385) but not these five arms.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| delete `contract.devices.read` arm | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| delete `contract.devices.create` arm | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| delete `contract.process.signals` arm | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| delete `contract.kernel.proc_read` arm | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline (clean tree + new test): PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-instance --lib override_policy_channels`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

name: instance-parse-field-duplicate-bit-table
title: tests(instance): pin parse_field duplicate-detection bits for contract allow/deny
body:
### What
Pins the `seen` bitmap bits used by `parse_field` for `[contract] allow` (bit 19) and `deny` (bit 20): repeating either key must fail with `DuplicateField`, while a single occurrence parses cleanly.

### Why it matters
`builder.mark(1 << N)` is the only duplicate guard. Shifting right (`1 >> 19 == 0`) marks bit 0, already seen from `schema_version`, so every config carrying `allow`/`deny` would be rejected as a duplicate of the wrong field. The existing duplicate test only pins `instance.id` (bit 1).

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `mark(1 << 19)` -> `mark(1 >> 19)` (contract.allow) | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `mark(1 << 20)` -> `mark(1 >> 20)` (contract.deny) | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline (clean tree + new test): PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-instance --lib parse_field_duplicate_detection`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

name: vfs-index-empty-and-link-boundary
title: tests(vfs): pin Index::is_empty and the symlink link-length boundary
body:
### What
Pins two VFS index guards: `Index::is_empty` reports true only for a zero-record index, and `Index::resolve` accepts a symlink whose target length equals the link buffer (`MAX_PATH`) exactly — the copy gate is `>` not `>=`.

### Why it matters
An inverted or constant-folded `is_empty` misreports index state to callers sizing iteration. Relaxing the link-length gate to `>=` rejects valid exact-fit targets. Existing tests never build an empty index nor an exact-MAX_PATH link.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `count == 0` -> `count != 0` (is_empty) | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `is_empty -> true` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| link-length gate `>` -> `>=` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline (clean tree + new test): PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-vfs --lib index_is_empty_and_resolve_link`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

name: fs-policy-rights-bit-positions
title: tests(fs-policy): pin Rights constants to exact distinct bit positions
body:
### What
Pins every `Rights` constant to its exact bit position (LOOKUP=1<<0 … EXECUTE=1<<5) and asserts pairwise non-containment so no two rights collapse onto the same bit.

### Why it matters
Capability checks are bitwise: shifting a constant right (`1 >> 3 == 0`) turns CREATE into the empty right that authorizes nothing, while colliding bits silently grant extra permissions. The existing `rights_contains_requires_every_requested_bit` test is shift-invariant (it only checks containment algebra), so it survives every `<<`->`>>` mutation.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `CREATE: 1 << 3` -> `1 >> 3` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `METADATA: 1 << 4` -> `1 >> 4` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `EXECUTE: 1 << 5` -> `1 >> 5` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline (clean tree + new test): PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-fs-policy --lib rights_constants_pin_exact`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.
spec_ref: capability rights bitmask contract (distinct single-bit rights)

name: devices-network-view-minor-and-ring-wrap
title: tests(devices): pin network view minor numbering and receive ring wrap order
body:
### What
Pins two device behaviors: network `views` project major 0 with one-based minors (`slot index + 1`), and `IsolatedNetwork::receive` advances the ring head with modulo wrap so FIFO order survives a full wrap cycle.

### Why it matters
The minor number identifies the network interface to userspace; `index + 1` mutated to `index * 1` or `index - 1` shifts every interface id. The receive head `(head + 1) % FRAMES` mutated to `/` breaks wrap-around and returns stale frames. Existing view tests only cover pseudo-devices; existing receive tests never wrap the ring.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `index as u32 + 1` -> `index as u32 * 1` (network minor) | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `index as u32 + 1` -> `index as u32 - 1` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `(head + 1) % FRAMES` -> `(head + 1) / FRAMES` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline (clean tree + new test): PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-devices --lib network_view_minor_is_one_based`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.
spec_ref: device view projection contract (network minor numbering); ring-buffer FIFO semantics
